summary: A form that validates, reports errors where the user can act on them, and survives a failed submit.
useWhen: collecting more than one field from the user before an action takes effect
the submit can fail server-side — which is every real form
structure: Fields in a single column. Two columns only for genuinely paired values, and they stack below the mobile breakpoint.
Each field carries its own label and, when invalid, its own errorMessage — the message sits with the control it is about.

Guidance needed to fill a field in goes in its `description`, always visible. An explanation most people will not need — why a limit exists, where to read more — goes in a Toggletip right after the label text, where it can hold a link.

Related fields that answer one question — an address, a pair of limits, a set of checkboxes — sit in a Fieldset, CheckboxGroup or RadioGroup, so the question is announced with each field and a group-level error has somewhere to live.

Choices that form a hierarchy — folders, teams within departments — are one TreeView with `selectionMode="multiple"` and an `aria-label` naming the question, not Checkboxes indented by hand. The tree announces each choice's level and place; indentation alone announces nothing.
An error summary Alert above the form after a failed submit, listing each invalid field as a link to it.

The actions in a ButtonGroup at the end: cancel first, the submit Button last — the primary last, as every action row in the system has it, so it is reached after the options it is chosen over and sits at the end of the row. `stack` on a form a phone will fill.

One value on a page that is read far more often than changed — a record's name or description — is an InlineEdit where it stands, not a form of one field: Edit, then Save or Cancel, with `validate` for its rule. Several values that belong together are still a form with one submit.

loading.must: Disable the submit Button and say what is happening on it — "Saving…" — rather than swapping the form for a spinner.
loading.why: the user needs to see what they typed while it is being saved, and a disabled control with unchanged text reads as broken
loading.a11y: announce the outcome in a live region; a disabled button cannot hold focus to be read

empty.must: A form's empty state is its initial state: no field shows an error before the user has touched it.
empty.why: validating on mount marks a form the user has not filled in as wrong, which teaches them to ignore the errors

error.must: Two levels, both required. Per-field `errorMessage` with `isInvalid`, plus an error summary Alert naming every failed field. Never clear what the user typed.
error.why: the summary is how a screen-reader or zoomed user finds the failures without hunting the whole form; the per-field message is how they fix each one
error.a11y: move focus to the summary after a failed submit — Alert's error intent already carries role="alert"

partial.must: When the server accepts some fields and rejects others, keep every value and mark only what failed.
partial.why: re-entering accepted data is the fastest way to lose a user mid-form

requires: a visible `label` on every field, or `aria-label` where the label is genuinely elsewhere
`isInvalid` alongside `errorMessage` — the message alone styles the field without announcing it as invalid
focus moved to the error summary after a failed submit
`isRequired` on required fields rather than an asterisk in the label text
a group-level error on the CheckboxGroup, RadioGroup or Fieldset it is about — "choose at least one" belongs to the set, not to its first box
notes: Validate on blur and on submit, not on every keystroke: an error that appears while the user is still typing the value is wrong more often than right.

antiPatterns.dont: clearing fields after a failed submit
antiPatterns.why: it punishes the user for the server's answer

antiPatterns.dont: an error summary with no per-field messages, or per-field with no summary
antiPatterns.why: each solves a different problem — finding the failures, and fixing one

antiPatterns.dont: a disabled submit Button as the only validation feedback
antiPatterns.why: the user is told no and never told why; a disabled button also takes no focus, so it cannot explain itself

antiPatterns.dont: placeholder text in place of a label
antiPatterns.why: it disappears on focus, which is exactly when it is needed, and it is not reliably announced

antiPatterns.dont: a Toggle inside a form that is submitted
antiPatterns.why: a switch says the change already took effect

antiPatterns.dont: a row of Checkboxes under a heading, with the error in a paragraph beneath
antiPatterns.why: the heading is not announced with the boxes and the error is attached to none of them

antiPatterns.dont: a Tooltip beside a label holding a link or the rule the field is validated against
antiPatterns.do: `description` for the rule; a Toggletip for the optional explanation and its link
antiPatterns.why: a tooltip is unreachable by keyboard and invisible on touch, so required guidance in one is found by failing

antiPatterns.dont: a CheckboxGroup whose boxes are indented with margins to show which folder each file is in
antiPatterns.why: the indentation is visual only: a screen reader hears one flat list, and there is no way to close a branch that is not wanted

antiPatterns.dont: a record's name as a button that turns into a field and saves on blur
antiPatterns.why: the value is announced as a button, and tabbing away to check something commits a half-typed value
